[Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) prove that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model ordering relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation; experiments confirm this for top-heavy metrics. Thus HR@10 against 99 negatives measures success within that candidate set. Uniform negatives can underrepresent popular competitors when catalogs have long tails, making popularity-based ranking appear effective; the direction and magnitude depend on sampling and interaction distributions, as investigated in [offline-evaluation experiments](https://doi.org/10.1145/3545796). Sampling bias and biased logged positives are distinct problems.

Recommended analysis: retain each model’s per-user binary hit on identical pinned candidates. Compute paired differences, then bootstrap 200 users independently within each dataset, preserving model pairing; average the four dataset means in every replicate for a 95% macro-difference interval. Report category intervals and win/loss/tie counts; paired randomization provides a complementary comparison. This applies [paired-resampling principles](https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/P18-1128.pdf). Define popularity exclusively from training interaction counts, including zero-count items; freeze category-specific head/mid/tail boundaries. Report validation target counts and paired HR changes by popularity stratum, plus a training-popularity baseline. For full-catalog unseen-item recommendations, report mean log-popularity, head share, coverage and concentration. Treat the 20 simulator users as descriptive only.

These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints, fixed candidate draws and observed users; they omit training-seed, candidate-sampling and split uncertainty. Repeated adaptive checkpoint/trial selection creates optimism that ordinary bootstrap intervals do not remove ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Record search breadth, label validation comparisons exploratory, and reserve confirmation for the host’s untouched final evaluation. Keep the pinned benchmark unchanged; sampled gains and popularity diagnostics cannot establish full-catalog accuracy, causal preference, intent improvement or unobserved diversity/conformity traits.
